entities.summary: Andrés de Urdaneta, OSA was a Basque maritime explorer for the Spanish Empire who later became an Augustinian friar. Born into a wealthy family in the Basque region of Spain, Urdaneta's early life was marked by a strong sense of adventure and a desire to explore the world's oceans. In 1535, he joined the Spanish Navy and quickly rose through the ranks, becoming a skilled navigator and cartographer. Urdaneta's most notable achievement was his discovery of the Pacific Ocean's passage to the Spice Islands in 1521, which he completed using a new navigational technique developed by his mentor, Martín de Argüelles. This discovery opened up a new trade route for the Spanish Empire and cemented Urdaneta's place in history as one of the greatest navigators of the 16th century. However, Urdaneta's life was not without controversy, as he was accused of piracy and treason by his fellow Spaniards. After being exonerated, Urdaneta returned to Spain and later became an Augustinian friar, devoting his life to prayer and service. His legacy as a pioneering navigator and explorer continues to inspire generations of sailors and historians alike.

entities.summary:
Andrés de Urdaneta, OSA was a Basque maritime explorer for the Spanish Empire who later became an Augustinian friar.

Born on November 30, 1498, in Ordizia, Spain, Urdaneta was part of a generation of skilled navigators and cartographers who contributed to the Age of Exploration.

Urdaneta's most notable achievement was leading the first expedition to circumnavigate the globe without a specific destination in mind, a feat that showcased his exceptional navigational skills and laid the groundwork for future Spanish maritime expeditions.

Following his expedition, Urdaneta returned to Spain and became an Augustinian friar, dedicating his life to the study of theology and the exploration of the New World.

His legacy as a pioneering explorer and later as a devout friar has left a lasting impact on the world, inspiring generations of sailors, cartographers, and theologians.

Like Columbus, Urdaneta's journey marked the beginning of a new era of global exploration and discovery, forever changing the course of human history.

The Viceroyalty of New Spain, established by the Spanish Crown in 1535, would go on to play a significant role in the colonization of the Americas, and Urdaneta's expedition would serve as a model for future Spanish explorers.

In recognition of his achievements, Urdaneta was awarded the title of Captain General of the Navies of the Indies, a testament to his status as one of the most accomplished explorers of his time.

Urdaneta's remarkable story serves as a reminder of the power of human ingenuity and perseverance in the face of uncertainty and danger.

The legacy of Andrés de Urdaneta continues to inspire new generations of explorers, scholars, and historians, a testament to the enduring impact of his remarkable journey.

As a symbol of the Age of Exploration, Urdaneta's name is etched in the annals of history, a reminder of the courage and determination that defined this pivotal moment in human history.
